title: Intersection and local detection calculus for subterminal module slices
statement:
Let $(\mathcal E,J)$ be a small subcanonical site with finite limits, let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and let $U,V\hookrightarrow1$ be subterminal objects such that $\{U,V\}\to1$ covers; put $W=U\times V$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] on the localized ringed sites [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Write $j_Z^*$ for restriction to $\mathcal E/Z$, and $k_U^*,k_V^*$ for restriction from $\mathcal E/U,\mathcal E/V$ to $\mathcal E/W$. For $Z=U,V,W$, the functor $j_Z^*$ has an additive exact left adjoint $j_{Z!}$, and both $j_Z^*$ and $j_{Z!}$ are exact. Explicitly $j_{Z!}F=P_F^\#$, where $P_F(C)=F(C\to Z)$ if there is a morphism $C\to Z$, and $P_F(C)=0$ otherwise, with scalar action induced by $R(C)$ [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. The same notation $k_{U!},k_{V!}$ denotes extension within a slice. There are natural module-linear identifications
$$j_U^*j_{U!}\cong1,\quad j_U^*j_{V!}\cong k_{U!}k_V^*,\qquad j_V^*j_{V!}\cong1,\quad j_V^*j_{U!}\cong k_{V!}k_U^*.$$
These identifications commute with units, counits, and the nested-open maps defined by adjunction; restriction commutes with the sheafification in the displayed presheaf formulas. The pair $(j_U^*,j_V^*)$ jointly detects zero module sheaves and exactness of module sequences. On complexes and ordinary derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], exact restriction commutes with every $H^q$, jointly detects cohomological vanishing and quasi-isomorphisms, and restriction and extension by zero act termwise as triangulated functors.

proof.text: Use localizedSystemExtension and localizedSystemRestriction with their proved exactness instances and the normalized localizedSystemAdjunction. For a subterminal Z, cancellation against Z → 1 makes Hom(X,Z) a subsingleton. The direct sum is zero when this type is empty; evaluation at any existing index is a linear equivalence with inverse the summand inclusion. This proves the stated presheaf formula with its specified generators.

source.place: Tags 03DI and 03DJ; specialization of the direct sum to a subsingleton index

proof.text: For a continuous and cocontinuous functor, restrict the module sheafification unit and transpose under source sheafification. Cocontinuity preserves its local bijectivity; localization identifies its sheafification as invertible, and the sheafification counit is invertible. Naturality follows by applying the adjunction hom equivalence. The same equivalence pins the comparison on unit images. Apply this independently universe-polymorphic argument to Over.forget and Over.map. This directly proves the required normalized comparisons.

source.place: Tag 04B8; normalized comparison by module-sheafification localization

proof.text: The singleton-summand inclusions define a presheaf isomorphism from F to restriction of its extension presheaf when Z is subterminal. Compose it with the restricted sheafification unit. The normalized adjunction identifies this composite with its unit. It is locally bijective and is a map between sheaves, hence invertible. Define the self-restriction comparison as the inverse of this unit.

source.place: Tag 0F6Z; singleton summand and the normalized unit

proof.text: For f:A→B with B subterminal, set k! = j_A! followed by j_B*. Restriction j_B* has the standard right adjoint along Over.star B. The functors Over.map f and Over.forget A followed by Over.star B are naturally isomorphic: on each object the inverse is the second projection, and subterminality gives the other inverse equation. Transporting the composite adjunction gives k! ⊣ f*. The extension is exact as a composite; f* is additive as its right adjoint, left exact as a right adjoint, and right exact by the standard adjunction f* ⊣ overPullback.

source.place: Tags 03DI and 04IY; composition of adjunctions and subterminality

proof.text: Let θ: j_V* followed by g* ≅ j_U* followed by f* be the canonical restriction comparison. Define the inverse exchange as its inverse mate under j_V! ⊣ j_V* and k_U! ⊣ f*. Mate θ again under the standard right adjoints of j_U* and g*. At Y→V its component is restriction of a module along the canonical slice isomorphism Y×_V W ≅ U×Y, for W=U×V. Its inverse is constructed by the product and pullback universal properties. Thus this second mate is invertible. The iterated-mate/conjugation theorem reflects its invertibility to the exchange map. The unit and counit mate identities give exactly the required normalized exchange equations. Repeat with U,V interchanged.

source.place: Tags 03DI and 0F6Z; agent categorical intersection calculation by iterated mates

proof.text: Define k_U! followed by j_U! ≅ j_W! by uniqueness of left adjoints after transporting the right adjoint through the canonical restriction isomorphism. The uniqueness unit equation is the required composition normalization. Transpose the nested map: it equals the inverse composition comparison followed by j_U! of k_U! applied to the inverse restriction comparison and then the k_U counit. Self-comparison naturality proves the self equation. The global triangle identities prove nested followed by counit equals the global W counit. The normalized composition units and the invertible global units imply each k-unit is invertible. For maps out of kX into kRY, postcomposition with its counit is injective: transpose and cancel R of the counit, which is invertible by the triangle identity. Apply this to the cross equation; after composing with the exchange counit, both sides reduce to restriction of the global W counit, using the self equation just proved. This proves both cross equations.

source.place: Tags 03DI and 04IY; adjunction uniqueness, triangles and mate identities

proof.text: A morphism whose U and V restrictions vanish is zero: on each object, use the cover by arrows whose domains map to U or V; naturality makes the restricted morphism zero and sheaf separatedness gives equality. Applying this to the identity detects zero objects. The product of the restriction functors is faithful by subtracting morphisms. It preserves finite limits and colimits; faithfulness therefore reflects monomorphisms and epimorphisms and hence isomorphisms in the abelian module category.

source.place: Agent cover-separatedness argument, as in the original node

proof.text: For a short complex, exactness is vanishing of its homology. The standard exact-functor homology comparison and joint zero detection give the exactness test. Use mapHomologicalComplexHomologyIso for all integer cohomology degrees; the same zero test gives cohomological vanishing, and joint isomorphism reflection gives the quasi-isomorphism test on homology maps. Exact functors act triangulated on ordinary unbounded derived categories with their Q-factorization. Use the proved source-library mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso to obtain all derived comparisons, derived vanishing and isomorphism tests. No boundedness hypothesis is used.

One commit. The item's statement, stmt_deps and blueprint fields are byte-identical to live, there are no new nodes, proof_deps equals the union of uses, and no SGA is cited. I read every cited statement. lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact gives exact j^* and j_! and the Hom bijection for any object and comm ring sheaf. The special-case clause of def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf (at most one map to U) applies because Z and W are subterminal. lem-weil-pbc-module-sheafification-restriction needs continuous and cocontinuous functors between small sites; step 2 checks this for the slice forgetful functor, and it gives the unit-normalized comparison. The exact-functor H^q, homology and triangulated results are mathlib leaves. Step by step: (3) the restricted P_F equals F (module version of 0F6Z). (4) An arrow C→V is the same as the unique arrow C→W=U×V over U, so the presheaves agree before sheafification; the k_V^* value comes from relocalization. (5) The unit and counit are determined on summand generators; I checked j_U^*ε_V against the k_U counit. (6) Nested maps use uniqueness of left adjoints and relocalization. (7) The pulled-back cover {C×U,C×V} plus sheaf separation proves zero and zero-morphism detection, with no points used. (8) Homology detection. (9) H^q commutes with restriction, giving quasi-isomorphism detection and unbounded triangulated functors. Edge cases tested: U=V=1, U=1, disjoint U and V, objects locally but not globally over V (sheafification is taken before identification), zero ring. reviewed_lean.note: Clause-by-clause check of Q93 5c1a9577 against the node. jstar, jbang and adj are the actual localizedSystem restriction, the sheafified extensionByZeroPresheaf extension, and the unit-normalized adjunction (.choose of an ∃!). Intersection presents kU and kV through adjunctions to overMap f and g. selfU/V (inv = unit), exchangeU/V (fixed by kU ⊣ f^* transposition), composeU/V (fixed by the composite unit) and the nested self/cross/counit equations are pinned and were checked consistent by hand, including exchange_counit through the triangle identity. PresheafFormula pins the DirectSum.of injection. Both sheafification-restriction comparisons are unit-normalized. JointDetection covers zero objects, zero maps, short exact sequences, H^q, QuasiIso and derived H^q/IsIso. DerivedExact gives triangulated mapDerivedCategory for jstar, jbang, kU, kV and overMap. Hypotheses: finite limits, subcanonical, Mono terminal.from, Bool ofArrows sieve in J(⊤), W = U⨯V; independent site universes, no extra assumptions. Edge cases U=V, U=1, disjoint, zero ring and all q are covered.
